patterns.usage_note: Marks an action carried on at the same time as the main action, attached to the ます-stem: 音楽を聞きながら歩く, one subject for both, with the ながら clause backgrounded. A sibling entry takes the concessive reading, although (知っていながら, 新人ながら), the usual sense after an adjective or a noun. After a noun, ながらの and ながらに name a state kept unchanged (昔ながらの町, 生まれながらに), a fixed set rather than a productive pattern.

examples.ruby: 音楽[おんがく]を聞[き]きながら走[はし]るのが日課[にっか]になっている。
examples.english: Running with music on has become part of my daily routine.

examples.ruby: 友[とも]だちは電話[でんわ]しながら、ノートに地図[ちず]を書[か]いていた。
examples.english: My friend drew a map in her notebook while talking on the phone.

examples.ruby: 味[あじ]を見[み]ながら少[すこ]しずつ塩[しお]を足[た]していった。
examples.english: I added the salt little by little, tasting as I went.

patterns.usage_note: Two actions at once by a single subject, taking the ます-stem: the written-language counterpart of ながら — 山道を登りつつ, 意見を参考にしつつ. In modern prose the concessive reading, "even while, although", dominates, especially with verbs of thinking or knowing (悪いと知りつつ); つつも makes that reading explicit. 〜つつある is a different pattern, saying a change is in progress.

examples.ruby: 体[からだ]に悪[わる]いと知[し]りつつ、つい夜更[よふ]かしをしてしまう。
examples.english: Knowing full well it's bad for me, I still end up staying up late.

examples.ruby: 険[けわ]しい山道[やまみち]を登[のぼ]りつつ、父[ちち]は昔[むかし]の話[はなし]を始[はじ]めた。
examples.english: As he climbed the steep mountain path, my father began telling stories of the old days.

examples.ruby: 専門家[せんもんか]の意見[いけん]を参考[さんこう]にしつつ、計画[けいかく]を練[ね]り直[なお]した。
examples.english: Drawing on expert opinion, we reworked the plan.
